questions.q: What does historical scenario replay do?
options: Applies the exact market moves from a real past crisis to the portfolio held today
Generates thousands of purely random future scenarios
Shocks only one risk factor while holding all others fixed
Predicts the next financial crisis before it happens
questions.explain: Historical scenario replay takes real historical market moves (e.g. 2008 or 2020) and applies them to the current portfolio, which is historically grounded but inherently backward-looking.

questions.q: How does sensitivity analysis differ from a full hypothetical scenario?
options: Sensitivity analysis can only be used on bond portfolios
Sensitivity analysis shocks one risk factor at a time, while a hypothetical scenario constructs a plausible combination of moves across multiple factors
Sensitivity analysis is always more accurate than scenario analysis
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: Sensitivity analysis isolates exposure to a single factor by holding everything else fixed, which is useful but ignores how multiple factors might move together, unlike a constructed hypothetical scenario.

questions.q: What question does reverse stress testing ask?
options: Given a specific scenario, what loss would result?
Given an unacceptable loss, what combination of market moves would be needed to cause it?
What was the largest historical loss this portfolio has ever experienced?
How does this portfolio compare to its benchmark index?
questions.explain: Reverse stress testing flips ordinary stress testing around: it starts from a specific unacceptable loss and works backward to identify what scenario would produce it, often surfacing hidden concentrations.

Types of exotic options
The Federal Reserve's standardized US bank stress-testing programs
Historical VaR calculation models
questions.explain: CCAR (Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review) and DFAST (Dodd-Frank Act Stress Test) are Federal Reserve programs that run large US banks through standardized adverse macroeconomic scenarios.

questions.q: What is a key limitation of historical scenario replay as a stress-testing method?
options: It is too computationally expensive to ever run
It can only be used for currency portfolios
It can only replay crises that have already happened, so it is backward-looking by construction
It always produces a smaller loss estimate than Monte Carlo simulation
questions.explain: Because historical replay is built from real past events, it is inherently limited to scenarios that have already occurred, unlike hypothetical scenarios which can probe entirely new, forward-looking risks.
